q: Williams' conjecture (1973) about SFTs was disproved by Kim–Roush (1992). The conjecture stated that two SFTs are conjugate iff:
opts: They have the same topological entropy
Their transition matrices are related by strong shift equivalence over ℤ
They have the same zeta function
They have the same number of periodic points at each period
exp: Williams conjectured: SFTs are conjugate iff shift equivalent (∃R,S with RS=A^n, SR=B^n and RA=BR, AS=SB over ℤ). Kim–Roush showed this fails — there are shift-equivalent but non-conjugate SFTs. The isomorphism problem for SFTs remains open.
